hook_text: That bowl of pap? It is eight-minute-old sunlight, stored for months in a mealie.
clip_script: Light leaves the Sun and crosses 150 million kilometres in about eight minutes. It lands on a mealie leaf in the Free State. Chlorophyll catches it and uses it to stitch carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, giving off the oxygen you are breathing now. The plant packs that sugar into its grains as stored energy. The farmer harvests, the mill grinds, you cook. When you eat it, your cells release that ancient sunlight to move your muscles and warm your body. Same story for the cow eating grass and the hawk eating the frog. Almost every bite on Earth started as sunshine.
visual_style: Whiteboard arrow from a cartoon Sun to a mealie leaf, CO₂ and water arrows going in, oxygen coming out, then a cob, a pot of pap and a person running, with a food chain of grass, cow and person below.
pacing: Quirky hook, a smooth journey, a big-picture finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace your lunch back to the Sun.
